chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Do not come to the chicks in their nests, nor the bird during its sleep until morning.' A man said to him: 'And what is its sleep, O Messenger of Allah?' He said: 'The night is its sleep, so do not hunt it during its sleep until morning, and do not come to the chick in its nest until it has grown feathers and flies. So when it flies, then aim your bow at it, and set up your net for it.'
ai.seo_question: What are the Islamic rules regarding hunting birds and when is it permissible?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi emphasizes the principle of *adab* (etiquette) in hunting by prohibiting the disturbance of birds in their nests or during their night sleep, defining night as their time of rest. It establishes a condition of fairness and maturity, requiring the bird to have grown feathers and be capable of flight before the hunter engages, reflecting the Shia scholarly emphasis on mercy and justice in permissible acts. This practice aligns with the Prophetic tradition of avoiding *ghubn* (deception or unfair advantage) in sport.
